script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for July 7. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Edison failed 1,000 times.  Rowling was rejected 12 times.  Colonel Sanders was rejected 1,009 times before KFC took off.

Every worthwhile goal has a 'dip'—a difficult period after initial enthusiasm fades. Most people quit in the dip. But the dip is a filter—it weeds out competition. Those who push through emerge with less competition on the other side. Persistence is easier with momentum.  Break big goals into small wins.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Most people quit too early.  Persistence teaches that the prize often goes to whoever stays longest.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Dip Check - Are You Close?.

Here's your activity: Think of something you've wanted to quit. Ask: Am I in the dip (temporary difficulty) or at a dead end (fundamentally wrong path)? If it's the dip, identify one small win you can achieve this week to build momentum. This helps you evaluate whether to persist or pivot.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about keeping going when it's hard can be applied to dip check - are you close?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
